title: gen-8 attach the consequence chosen by C-002's record to blackboard.py, and publish the act
description: Implement in .harness/bin/blackboard.py exactly the alternative that the record disposing C-002 adopted (read the record: precedent.py show <id> or the JSON in .harness/precedents/), on top of T-422's scaffold. Whatever the alternative: ties and unranked fall back to (priority, id); closed gate keeps today's order with the printed reason; no write to anything reputation.py owns; named refusal/yield events in events.jsonl; the rename bypass documented in the docstring. Tests in test_blackboard_next_ordering.py for the consequence, for the fallback, and a mutation check that the consequence disappears when the gate closes. Then satisfy PR-060 clause 6: publish a declarative record (precedent.py publish, --agent registro-a, --follows the C-002 record, sources decision:T-426 and the code path) that names the operational parameter, the consequence, and this act of setting it. Standing rules: claim with blackboard.py claim <ID> --agent <you>; lock every file you edit with lock.py acquire; no emojis; nothing tracked may contain user paths, sibling-project names or personal tooling; never sign anything; never touch .harness/keys, trust/, constitutional/; never route around prevent_data_loss.py; commit is done by the coordinator, not you; hand off with blackboard.py handoff <ID> --agent <you> --to-role verifier with replayable evidence (exact commands + expected output). verifier-g8-attach: starting adversarial verify (a)-(g) per T-427 spec

VERIFIED (round 1, adversarial replay + independent black-box CLI attack, cognitive diversity from producer's white-box unittest approach): attacks (a)-(g) all PASS.

(a) rename bypass, MUST work + documented: replayed via real `blackboard.py next` CLI subprocess against a fresh scratch harness root (<session-scratchpad>/t427-attack-*) with a real ed25519 keypair, enrolled trust anchor, and a real ssh-keygen-signed constitutional file (activation on). worker-y (0.0 score) requesting next against worker-x (holds an active precedent, nonzero score) yields: exit 2, "yield: worker-y is outranked by live candidate 'worker-x'...", one phase_b_yield event logged. Requesting `next --agent worker-x` (the top identity) then never yields: exit 0, no yield line -- confirms the bypass is real and reproducible, and it is documented (not hidden) in `phase_b_yield_check`'s own docstring, section "RENAME BYPASS". Repro: `python3 <workspace>/.harness/bin/blackboard.py next --agent worker-y --role worker` vs `--agent worker-x` against the scratch root with PR-900 authored by worker-x.

(b) gate closed mid-run: same fixture/data, baseline yields (exit 2). Renamed `constitutional/reputation.json.sig` away (unsigned) mid-run -> exit 0, no "yield:" line, reason printed verbatim: "phase-b claim order not applied: UNSIGNED -- no detached signature at <path>". Restored the .sig -> yield returns (exit 2) on the identical data, proving the consequence is gated on the signed file and not innate to the score.

(c) ties: gave worker-x and worker-y each one authored precedent (equal total_score) -> exit 0, no yield line, no phase_b_yield event -- falls back to today's (priority, id) order. Separately confirmed the underlying task-selection fallback itself: T-2 (priority 1) picked over T-9 (priority 1) by id ordering, unaffected by phase-b.

(d) unknown identity never crashes: tried a fresh never-seen identity (exit 2, correctly outranked, no crash), a quote-embedded identity `weird"name'x` (exit 2, no crash), and an identity containing a literal comma `weird,name` -- this one exposed that the --candidates CSV join (pre-existing T-422 seam, not part of T-426's own diff) splits on the comma, so the agent string fails to exact-match any split identity; `phase_b_yield_check`'s "requester_score is None" branch fires and the call fails safe: exit 0, no yield, no crash. Noted for the record as a pre-existing CSV-join quirk in the identity seam (not introduced by T-426, and it fails closed/safe rather than mis-yielding), not a T-426 defect.

(e) zero unauthorized writes: sha256-hashed every file under precedents/, constitutional/, trust/, cases/, plus blackboard.json and state.json before and after a `next` call that yields -- identical hashes on all of them; only logs/events.jsonl grew (phase_b_yield row). Then hashed the same set around a `claim` call -- identical on everything except blackboard.json (claim's own task-state write), events.jsonl untouched. Matches "no write to anything reputation.py owns; only write is the phase_b_yield row" verbatim.

(f) c6 record: PR-063 relations=[{"type":"follows","target":"PR-062"}] (PR-062 is the record disposing C-002 -- "follows the C-002 record" is satisfied via the record that actually disposed the case, since a case itself cannot be a `follows` target in precedent.py's schema); `precedent.py cite --record PR-063` -> every token OK, zero dangling; `precedent.py conflicts` -> 0 findings across 63 records; ratio section (1)/(2)/(3) names the parameter (claim priority ordering), the consequence (YIELD-AT-NEXT verbatim, both non-adopted alternatives named), and the act (T-426, code path). C-003/PR-063 disposed correctly under T-412/S-1's mandatory case-per-publish rule (confirmed by reading precedent.py: "--case is required on every publish" and "a second disposal of one case is refused") -- opening a fresh case for the c6 record was the only mechanically valid shape, resolving the worker's own open item.

(g) exact match, replayed independently: `test_reputation.py` 41 passed, `test_reputation_phase_b.py` 32 passed (both files show zero git diff -- untouched). `test_blackboard_next_ordering.py` 53 passed.
